messages.subject: distsamp site level estimates
parts:
Hola

I am running null models with distsamp() to estimate density and abundance of Black-face Ibis. I need to clarify if density and/or abundance estimates correspond to transect/point level or to the all study area.

In previous posts I have read that results in null models correspond to transect/point level, in other posts results from null models correspond to the all study area and if you use covariate you will get estimates at plot site level.

All the best,

Adrian

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] distsamp site level estimates
parts:
Dear Adrian,

both are at the site-level ! To estimate abundance for the entire study area you must scale up, for instance, as we did in this publication:

Hierarchical distance‐sampling models to estimate population size and habitat‐specific abundance of an island endemic
TS Sillett, RB Chandler, JA Royle, M Kéry, SA Morrison
Ecological Applications 22 (7), 1997-2006

Don't be confused: whether you have a Null model or covariates for abundance has no importance for the interpretation of the abundance parameter, which is always for a site. In the case of a Null model, the expected abundance is identical for ALL sites, while in a model with covariates on abundance, the expected abundance at the site is simply a function of the covariate value at that site. In either case, to obtain an estimate of abundance in a wider study area you will have to scale up in some way.

Best regards  -- Marc
